title: Why Doctors Were Ordered to Wash Their Hands
topic: Ignaz Semmelweis and why doctors in 1847 Vienna were ordered to wash their hands (childbed fever)

lines: Ignaz Semmelweis ordered every student to scrub in bleach before touching a mother.
The other doctors were offended.
They were gentlemen. How could their hands be dirty?
But in their clinic, mothers were dying of childbed fever.
Three times more than in the midwives' clinic.
Women begged on their knees not to be sent there.
Some gave birth in the street instead, and rarely got the fever.
Then his friend Jakob Kolletschka was cut by a student's scalpel during an autopsy.
His body showed the same signs as the dying mothers.
You see, it's like cutting raw chicken, then making a salad without washing your hands.
Every morning, the doctors cut open women who had died the day before.
Then they went straight to the living mothers.
The midwives never touched a corpse.
So in May 1847, he ordered hand washing in chlorinated lime.
Deaths fell from 18% to less than 3%.
But his ideas were rejected and ridiculed.
In 1865, his colleagues committed him to an asylum, where guards beat him.
He died 14 days later from an infected wound on his hand.
Years later, Louis Pasteur's germ theory explained why he was right.
The doctor who told everyone to clean their hands died from an infected hand.
